questions: Do you also have chest pain or pressure (especially when you walk or exert yourself)?
Do you have any visible vulvar skin changes—such as redness, white patches, sores/ulcers, or a new lump—on exam or when you look?
Have you noticed any abnormal vaginal discharge (e.g., thick white “cottage cheese,” watery/gray, or foul-smelling discharge) along with the vulvar itching?
Have you noticed any white, thin, or “paper-like” patches or skin that tears easily on the vulva (even if subtle)?
Have you had any vulvar burning or pain when you urinate (dysuria), and/or do symptoms worsen with urine contact to the vulva?
Have you noticed any new or persistent vulvar skin thickening or changes in color/texture (such as a white patch, dark patch, or rough area) that would not go away?
Have you had any burning pain or bleeding at the vulva during sex or since menopause, and is the skin very thin/whitish or does it tear easily?
Have you noticed any new vaginal/vulvar odor or pain/burning specifically at the vaginal opening during urination or tampon insertion?
Have you ever had a vulvar biopsy or been evaluated by a gynecologist/dermatologist with a close vulvar exam (including checking for lichen sclerosus or other dermatoses)?
Have you noticed any vulvar skin changes over time—especially white thickened patches, thin “paper-like” skin, fissures (small tears), or easy bruising/tearing?
answers: Patient: No, I don’t have chest pain or pressure when I walk or exert myself. My main problem is severe vulvar itching and pain with sex that’s been getting worse over the past year.
“No, when I look there aren’t any new lumps or open sores. I do notice the area looks a bit red and irritated, but I haven’t seen distinct white patches or anything ulcerated.”

“No, I haven’t noticed any unusual discharge—no thick white ‘cottage cheese,’ no watery or gray fluid, and no strong or foul smell. The itching is the main issue, and it’s also worse with sex due to the pain.”
“I haven’t noticed any white, thin ‘paper-like’ patches or skin that tears easily, though the vulvar area does seem more red and sensitive, especially with friction during sex.”

“No, I don’t have burning when I urinate. I haven’t noticed that my vulvar symptoms get worse specifically from urine contact—mainly it’s the itching and the pain during sex, especially with friction.”

“I haven’t noticed any persistent thickening or rough, dark, or clearly defined color changes that don’t go away. It mostly stays red and irritated and feels very sensitive, especially during and after sex.”

“No, I haven’t noticed vulvar burning beyond the itching and pain with sex, and I’ve had no bleeding. The tissue doesn’t seem especially thin or whitish to me, and I haven’t noticed that it tears easily—just that it’s very red, tender, and sensitive with friction.”

“No, I haven’t noticed any new odor, and when I urinate there isn’t specific burning at the vaginal opening. I also haven’t had any issues with tampon insertion—my main symptoms are the severe vulvar itching and the pain during sex with friction.”

“I have not had a vulvar biopsy. I’ve seen my gynecologist once about it, but I haven’t had a very detailed vulvar skin-focused exam or evaluation by a dermatologist specifically for conditions like lichen sclerosus.”

“I haven’t noticed any fissures or small tears, and I don’t see any white thickened or ‘paper-like’ patches. It’s mostly persistent redness and irritation with very tender, sensitive skin that flares with friction during sex.”
